target: Erdos #616 (r-uniform hypergraph covering number under a 3r-3 local condition)
headline: The stub's sorry'd goal is FALSE, and not only for arithmetic reasons. For 3 <= r <= 5 the optimum EXISTS and equals exactly 1 (below the claimed lower bound 3r/16+7/8). For every r >= 6 an explicit 4-edge family forces the optimum to be at least 2 (above the claimed upper bound r/5 whenever r < 10). Separately, the claimed window [3r/16+7/8, r/5] is empty for every r < 70.

open.typed: forall r : Nat, 6 <= r -> exists t : Q, Optimal r t
open.why: Optimal r t asserts t is the LEAST admissible bound. For 3 <= r <= 5 we exhibited it (= 1). For r >= 6 nothing here shows the supremum of tau over all n and all admissible H is even finite, so `Optimal r t` may be uninhabited for every t. Every r >= 6 result in this file is therefore phrased on `Good r t`, never on `Optimal r t`.

open.typed: forall r : Nat, 3 <= r -> Good r (((1:Q)/5) * r)
open.why: The genuine content of [EHT91] - that tau is bounded at all, by ~r/5 - is untouched. This file only shows the bound as transcribed is false for r in {3,4} and {6,...,9}; it says nothing for r >= 10, and in particular nothing about the r >= 70 range where the claimed window is nonempty.

open.typed: forall r : Nat, forall t : Q, Good r t -> ((3:Q)/16) * r + 7/8 <= t
open.why: Our construction is a single 4-edge family and only ever yields tau = 2, for every r >= 6. Reaching the EHT lower bound's linear growth in r needs a genuinely different (EHT-style) family; the hub-plus-block shape used here has transversal number exactly 2 no matter how many blocks are used.

open.typed: n/a - a modelling question, not a Lean goal
open.why: The refutation is of the stub AS WRITTEN, which quantifies the EHT inequalities over ALL r >= 3. The source page states them without a range; if [EHT91] intends them asymptotically (or for r large), the stub - not the literature - is what is wrong. Nothing in this file distinguishes those two readings, and the sealed r <= 5 values (optimum = 1) are evidence that the small-r regime is genuinely degenerate.
